  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Night: may deal a Basic Attack to one player.
  Only players your own Attack kills count (it counts even if another fatal Attack hit them too, R12); other deaths
  you cause (a trait's effect, a hanging) don't. Good means
  true alignment: a Village player, whatever alignment checks see (a Turncoat counts as Good, and so does a framed
  Villager; a Yakuza holding the Katana doesn't). At the end of each night your Attack kills someone, you are told
  whether they were Good. Night deaths are simultaneous (R10): a player you kill on the night you die still counts.
  Win: iff your Attacks kill 2 Good players. If you are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave
  the game (leaving works as for the Executioner). If you have died, you still win and nothing is revealed.
  Lose: as soon as your Attack kills a player who isn't Good; if you are alive, the moderator reveals you at once
  and you leave the game.

Chaos (Neutral roles that win by other means; Evil to the Sheriff, R19)

Jester
  Defense: Basic.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you are hanged during a Day (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if the game ends with you
  alive.
  Revenge: if you are hanged, the following night a random Guilty voter from your trial who was alive when that
  night began is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted Guilty, nothing happens.

Executioner
  Defense: Basic.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get a random target: any player except yourself.
  Win: iff your target is hanged during a Day while you are alive (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if
  the game ends with your target alive.
  On winning: the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game. Leaving works exactly like dying (you
  leave the circle for good) except it doesn't count as a death. The following night, a random Guilty voter from
  the trial who was alive when that night began (not you, since you left) is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted
  Guilty, nothing happens.
  If your target dies any other way, or leaves the game, you become a Jester.

Magpie
  Defense: Basic. Never blocks wins (R1). Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens.
  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

---

Which traits are dealt is drawn to help balance the sides; some traits can go only to Village players.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- An Eavesdropper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the eavesdrop op; code shows them the target's private messages tomorrow and tells them so at dawn. Don't tell() the Eavesdropper anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- Werewolf: on even-numbered Nights only, a Werewolf who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) rampages: at its target's house (a visit to them; put it in record_visits) or, with no target or itself as target, at home (not a visit). Call record_visits first, then the rampage op ({op:'rampage', by, player}, player left out for a home rampage): code lists the Strong Attacks it deals, cause 'Werewolf', from the recorded visits: on the target (a visit) and on every other player who visited the target (or, at home, the Werewolf) tonight, of any faction (not visits; Astral Visits aren't visits, so they aren't hit). Resolve each like any attack (Defense, Medics, charms, traps, mirrors: give the visit flag code gives). An Enforcer counts a rampage at a player's house, its hits on visitors included, as an Attack of the Werewolf's own choosing; a home rampage doesn't count. Tell the Werewolf how many players it attacked and how many of those attacks killed (an attack a mirror reflects back at the Werewolf isn't one of them), never who the visitors were (e.g. 'Your rampage attacked 3 players and killed 2 of them').
- Drowsy (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Drowsy player is role-blocked; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Bonded (a trait, R24): Alice and Frank. When one of a pair dies, code kills the other at once (cause heartbreak, not an attack). Never kill anyone for heartbreak yourself.
- Niaj (Drowsy) is not role-blocked by the trait tonight; code drew it.
- Olivia (Drowsy) is not role-blocked by the trait tonight; code drew it.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- An Eavesdropper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the eavesdrop op; code shows them the target's private messages tomorrow and tells them so at dawn. Don't tell() the Eavesdropper anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- Werewolf: on even-numbered Nights only, a Werewolf who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) rampages: at its target's house (a visit to them; put it in record_visits) or, with no target or itself as target, at home (not a visit). Call record_visits first, then the rampage op ({op:'rampage', by, player}, player left out for a home rampage): code lists the Strong Attacks it deals, cause 'Werewolf', from the recorded visits: on the target (a visit) and on every other player who visited the target (or, at home, the Werewolf) tonight, of any faction (not visits; Astral Visits aren't visits, so they aren't hit). Resolve each like any attack (Defense, Medics, charms, traps, mirrors: give the visit flag code gives). An Enforcer counts a rampage at a player's house, its hits on visitors included, as an Attack of the Werewolf's own choosing; a home rampage doesn't count. Tell the Werewolf how many players it attacked and how many of those attacks killed (an attack a mirror reflects back at the Werewolf isn't one of them), never who the visitors were (e.g. 'Your rampage attacked 3 players and killed 2 of them').
- Drowsy (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Drowsy player is role-blocked; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Niaj (Drowsy) is not role-blocked by the trait tonight; code drew it.
- Olivia has the hidden Drowsy trait (R24) and is role-blocked tonight; code drew it. Handle it exactly like a role-block (R9) with no blocker: their actions, automatic effects and trait actions have no effect and spend no tokens, they make no visit, and they are told they were role-blocked, as usual. Never mention the trait or say why.

reasoning:
I'm taking stock of who's alive and what threats remain — the werewolf that killed Judy, Alice, and Heidi is still at large, the Katana killed Dave and likely passed to someone new, and there's a Hitman factor to account for too.

Erin was killed by what looks like an Enforcer attack on N3, which fits Niaj's claim that he visited Erin and Grace — if both attacked, the Enforcer randomly picks one target. Since Alice was the confirmed Enforcer and died N2, Niaj's Enforcer claim checking out otherwise would require a second hidden Enforcer, so I'm leaning toward Niaj being genuinely good, especially combined with his N1 difference-check against Bob.

Now I'm wondering who role-blocked me N3 — that points toward a Pharmacist or Party Animal, with Pharmacist tied to Yakuza, and I'm trying to cross-reference that against the census results.

Narrowing suspects: Alice confirmed good leaves Bob and Mallory non-good from the N1 check, putting Mallory in the Neutral or Yakuza camp alongside Carol and Grace as remaining suspects, with the Werewolf likely hiding among them. I'm also weighing whether Erin was the Katana-wielding Yakuza (with Grace as partner) or the Hitman, which determines whether the Katana holder is still alive among Carol, Grace, or Mallory — and I'm starting to look at the Bob trial numbers from Day 3 for more clues.

Now with Mallory on trial, I'm considering her claim of Jester from Day 3 — real Jesters want to be hanged, so claiming Jester while fighting the nomination seems backwards unless it's reverse psychology, which makes me suspicious that she's actually the Werewolf trying to dodge the rope.

I recall the Werewolf rampaged at Judy's on N2, and Mallory's claim about no night action on Day 3 fits a Jester lacking actions on odd nights, which muddies things further. There's also a real risk: if Mallory actually is the Jester and we hang her, we'd lose someone to Guilty voting tonight plus the Werewolf kill plus Katana, potentially wiping the group down to a dangerously small number.

Looking at who'd remain—Carol, Grace, Niaj, and myself—the Werewolf is likely hiding among Carol or Grace, with Yakuza possibly being the other. That's a grim setup. If we skip the hang, the Werewolf among Carol/Grace/Mallory still rampages tonight regardless.

I'm weighing whether to pivot the hang toward Grace instead, since we only get one trial today unless someone's cleared Innocent, and with three max trials and five voters we'd need three Guilty votes to convict. Grace stands out because she's never claimed a role at all, which is suspicious, while Carol has an Auditor claim with no visits on N1 or N2—and their voting patterns on Mallory and Bob diverge in a way worth digging into further.

Bob himself was probably Yakuza, though I realize he could've been the Werewolf too, since the Werewolf's only confirmed kill was N2 and Bob was hanged D3 with no kill on the odd N3—so there's no guarantee a Werewolf is even still alive. Looking at the D3 Bob trial, I'm trying to pin down who voted Innocent among the seven, since Dave's Kindred claim confirms Niaj voted Guilty alongside him, narrowing it to Carol, Erin, Grace, or Mallory—and I'm considering whether Mallory exposing Bob's PM makes sense if she were aligned with him as Yakuza, or whether that points toward her being the Werewolf instead.

Checking the Bob nomination vote, I work out that Carol and Mallory must have voted Yes alongside Olivia, Niaj, and Dave, while Erin and Grace voted No, with Grace also trying to redirect suspicion onto Niaj. I'm also puzzling over Grace's N3 Enforcer visit to both Erin and Grace, wondering if Erin and Grace are actually the Hitman and Katana holder who attacked Dave, and trying to figure out who blocked me N3—possibly a Yakuza Pharmacist.

My top suspect is Grace, but today's vote is on Mallory. If the count lands Grace and Niaj Guilty, Mallory Innocent, it comes down to me and Carol. I'm weighing whether Mallory could be Jester, Werewolf, or Yakuza—her strong pushback against being hanged and her exposing Bob's deal make Jester seem unlikely, since a Jester wanting to win would've taken Bob's offer instead.

I'm also considering whether Grace might be pushing to hang Mallory as evil cover, wasting the day or baiting a Divine kill, and trying to track which evils remain alive—possible Yakuza among Bob, Erin, or Frank, whose bond to Alice and empty will still need accounting for.

With 3-4 Yakuza total in the setup, at least a couple should still be alive among Carol, Grace, or Mallory, alongside the Werewolf and up to two other Neutral killers like Hitman or a Jester (possibly Mallory). I'm trying to tally the confirmed Good roles—Alice, Ivan, Judy, Heidi, Dave, Niaj, and myself—to see how many slots remain for hidden evils.

Frank bonded, so he could be Yakuza, which would make Carol, Grace, and Mallory all suspect too — possibly all non-Good, though Carol stays plausible as Good if Frank turns out Yakuza.

If both Werewolf and Yakuza survive, the game drags on, and with only me and Niaj (plus maybe Carol) on the Village side, every hang counts. Mallory's confirmed non-Good by census, so hanging her removes an evil unless she's secretly the Jester, which would cost a Guilty voter instead — I'm weighing whether that's likely.

If Mallory were Jester, that'd push neutrals to three alongside the Werewolf and Hitman, meaning Yakuza would need 3-4 members to fill out the evil team, which would require Bob, Erin, Frank, Carol, Grace, and Mallory to all be non-Good — technically consistent with needing at least five Good non-Outsiders, but it stretches the typical setup of only two neutrals.

Erin might actually be the Hitman who killed Dave, which would explain why Erin's dead now, while Bob seems like a plausible Werewolf candidate. The Hitman needs two Good kills to survive undetected — Dave was one — so if the Hitman is still alive, one more Good kill would expose them. As the Seer with a token, I'm thinking about using tonight's check on a pair, factoring in the Werewolf's rampage on night four.

Leaning toward voting Guilty on Mallory since she's census-confirmed non-Good and doesn't fit the Jester profile, though if I'm wrong and she is the Jester, one of the guilty voters could die tonight. The alternative is pushing suspicion onto Grace instead, since she never claimed a role, and I'm weighing what Niaj's Enforcer visit to Grace on night three might have revealed.

I should also push Grace to finally claim her role, since she's the only one alive who hasn't. Trial order matters too — Mallory and Niaj already spoke, so I'm next, then Carol, which affects when Grace gets a chance to respond to pressure.

I'm leaning toward voting Guilty on Mallory. Dave's census plus her pattern of pleading for innocence then exposing Bob's deal both point to her not being a true Jester — a real Jester would've taken Bob's offer. That makes her Werewolf, Hitman, or Yakuza, any of which deserves the hang.

I should also pressure Grace, the only player who hasn't claimed a role yet, to reveal her claim and N1-N3 visits before the vote — and flag that Carol's and Niaj's visits to Erin and Grace on N3 make them a suspicious pair if Grace flips evil. I'll update my will with today's vote reasoning and add this to my notepad.

I'll draft a short public statement: vote Innocent again since Guilty risks a Divine revenge, and pivot attention to Grace's silence, pressing her to claim her role and early-night visits before the vote. That keeps my message within budget, so I'll update the notepad accordingly.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- An Eavesdropper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the eavesdrop op; code shows them the target's private messages tomorrow and tells them so at dawn. Don't tell() the Eavesdropper anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- Werewolf: on even-numbered Nights only, a Werewolf who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) rampages: at its target's house (a visit to them; put it in record_visits) or, with no target or itself as target, at home (not a visit). Call record_visits first, then the rampage op ({op:'rampage', by, player}, player left out for a home rampage): code lists the Strong Attacks it deals, cause 'Werewolf', from the recorded visits: on the target (a visit) and on every other player who visited the target (or, at home, the Werewolf) tonight, of any faction (not visits; Astral Visits aren't visits, so they aren't hit). Resolve each like any attack (Defense, Medics, charms, traps, mirrors: give the visit flag code gives). An Enforcer counts a rampage at a player's house, its hits on visitors included, as an Attack of the Werewolf's own choosing; a home rampage doesn't count. Tell the Werewolf how many players it attacked and how many of those attacks killed (an attack a mirror reflects back at the Werewolf isn't one of them), never who the visitors were (e.g. 'Your rampage attacked 3 players and killed 2 of them').
- Drowsy (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Drowsy player is role-blocked; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Niaj has the hidden Drowsy trait (R24) and is role-blocked tonight; code drew it. Handle it exactly like a role-block (R9) with no blocker: their actions, automatic effects and trait actions have no effect and spend no tokens, they make no visit, and they are told they were role-blocked, as usual. Never mention the trait or say why.
- Olivia (Drowsy) is not role-blocked by the trait tonight; code drew it.

Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:

Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.

output.confusing_rules: Three things. 1) Bonded (R24) says the partner is a 'random Village or Yakuza player', but it doesn't say clearly whether a Yakuza can be bonded to a Villager. Frank was bonded to Alice, an Enforcer, and that ruled out Katana kills and hangs on Alice. I had to work out from the text that cross-faction bonds are possible. 2) It wasn't clear what a Hitman's death message looks like, or that a hanged real Jester always gets a public win announcement (R12). Niaj caught the missing announcement only after Mallory was hanged. A clearer line, such as 'a hanged Jester is always announced', would help both sides plan their Jester bluffs. 3) The Drowsy and R9 wording: players get 'You were role-blocked' even with no blocker and even on nights they chose no action (Olivia on N6). It's correct, but the table read every block as proof of a hidden Pharmacist or Party Animal.
output.missing_information: As an Informant I had no easy record of each player's stated votes alongside the real votes I saw. I had to keep both in my notepad by hand. A per-trial log of what players said they voted, next to the private vote breakdown I was shown, would help. I also wasn't told whether a teammate's attack worked (that's by design), so after Erin died on N3 I had to infer what happened from the morning deaths.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to pass Informant vote data to the town without giving myself away. Mallory said in public she voted Guilty on Bob but actually voted Innocent. There's no way to use that lie without revealing the role. That's a fair limit, but it made my role mostly dead weight in a 4-person Yakuza with three Informants.
output.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The setup's balance looked off. Our 4-player Yakuza drew Wiretap plus three Informants: no blocker, no killing role besides the Katana, and three copies of the same passive information. Erin, Frank and I all got identical vote breakdowns. Against a Werewolf, a Hitman and two Enforcers, that is very weak. 2) Day 5-6 with 2 alive: Olivia nominated Carol five times, and with 1 Yes every nomination was hopeless. The day kept going until a full round of silence. It all seemed consistent with the rules. 3) Otherwise everything matched the rules text: the N2 rampage and heartbreak chain, the N3 Enforcer double visit, the N4 rampage at my house.
output.suggestions: Two changes. 1) Limit duplicate passive Yakuza roles (e.g. at most one Informant), or let the balancer count the overlap, since three Informants give no more information than one. 2) When only 2 players are alive and neither can reach a nomination majority, end the Day automatically or skip to Night.

output.confusing_rules:
1) Werewolf versus Enforcer. The rules say a Werewolf's rampage at another player's house counts as "an Attack of its own choosing", so an Enforcer who visits the Werewolf does attack it. But the Werewolf's Standard Defense means a free Basic Enforcer attack can never kill it. That only became clear by putting the Enforcer, Werewolf and R3 texts together. One line in the Enforcer text would help, such as "Basic can't get through Standard Defense; spend the Strong token on suspected Neutral killers".
2) On even nights, any visit to a random target risks getting caught in a rampage. That's what killed me on N2, and it's easy to overlook on the Enforcer's 'free' visit.
3) Bonded doesn't say whether my partner is on my side, only "Village or Yakuza". I had to treat Frank as a possible Yakuza the whole game and couldn't safely lean on him or push against him.
output.missing_information: Nothing was missing from the rules themselves. What was hard to track was every player's night visits, so I could work out which visits were safe on a full-moon night. A running per-night list of public visit claims, set against the visit counts that had been posted, would have helped. Once I was dead I had no view of the game until the end. That's fine, but it's worth noting.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: Before I died, I wanted a way to tell my Bonded partner something without making it public. Day 1 and Day 2 had no PMs at all, so any PM would have stood out. Otherwise none.
output.bugs_or_oddities:
1) The endgame stalled. From Day 5 only Carol (Werewolf) and Olivia (Village) were alive. A nomination needed 2 Yes votes, so nothing could ever pass, yet Olivia nominated five times over two Days and wasted turns until the Werewolf killed her on N6. This follows the rules, but it's a dead stretch of play.
2) The wording of night results isn't consistent. Carol's N2 result read "Your rampage attacked 3 players...", while her N4 result read "You rampaged at Grace's house tonight. Your rampage attacked 1...". The same goes for "You did not attack" (N1) versus "You didn't attack" (N2).
3) Everything else I checked fit the rules: Drowsy explains all the role-blocks with no blocker alive, and the census counts, the Seer pairs and the heartbreak death were all correct.
output.suggestions:
1) When a two-player game can't end by vote, skip straight to Night, or tell the players that nominations can't pass.
2) Use the same template for every night result.
3) Add a short role-interaction note to roles whose free action is weaker than it looks: the Enforcer's Basic attack against Standard Defense, and visiting on Werewolf nights.
4) Optionally, tell Bonded players whether their partner shares their faction. As it stands, the Yakuza used my bond to keep me safe (they knew Frank was theirs), while I knew nothing. That imbalance makes the trait a quiet gift to the Yakuza.

output.confusing_rules: Mostly clear. A few rough spots: (1) R4 says the Day ends after three passed nominations, but it doesn't say failed nominations are unlimited. With 2 players alive I could nominate Carol again and again at 1-1, which looked like I should be able to do something when nothing was possible. (2) The interaction between the hidden Drowsy trait and the Seer's automatic random pair is only stated indirectly, in R9 and R20 step 1. I first had to work out that a Drowsy Seer loses the free pair too, not just the chosen one. (3) R12 says a hanged Jester's win announcement names the role, so no announcement after Mallory's hang meant she wasn't a Jester. That's a strong rule, but it's buried, and in a live game it's easy to miss that the absence of an announcement is information.
output.missing_information: (1) A stall-rule countdown. I had to work out myself which night had to have a death to avoid everyone losing. (2) A per-player record of each player's stated vote next to the announced totals. I kept it by hand in the notepad, and with only 425 words that space was tight. (3) A visible note that my seer token can't do anything when fewer than two other players are alive. I only found out at night.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: On Night 3 I spent my token on the pair Erin/Dave, which would have shown Erin as Evil. Drowsy blocked it, and I had no way of knowing Drowsy existed until I was told I was role-blocked. That's within the rules, just frustrating. In the final 1v1 against a Werewolf with Standard Defense, nothing I could do mattered: hanging can't pass 1-1, and I had no attack. I wanted some way to act, or at least for the game to tell me the position was lost.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked inconsistent with the rules. Things I checked: my Night 3 token wasn't spent after the block (correct under R9); I was told I was role-blocked on Night 6 with no action submitted (consistent with Drowsy and R9); the game kept going after the last Yakuza died because the Werewolf blocks wins (correct). One odd thing: Bob, a fake Fortune Teller, posted N2 counts of 3 visited / 5 visitors that matched the real visits exactly. He did it with Wiretap and Katana knowledge plus a lucky guess, and it fooled several players for a while. Not a bug, but worth knowing.
output.suggestions: (1) When only 2 players are alive and neither has a day action that could change the result, end the Day after one round. Or warn the player that nominations can't pass, instead of letting five 1-1 nominations happen. (2) Show a stall-rule counter in the ledger, e.g. 'nights/days since last death: X of 3'. (3) Add a stated-vote column to the public ledger's trial entries, filled from players' [Claim] lines. (4) When a hanged player's role has a win announcement and none appears, state it explicitly, e.g. 'no win was announced'. That makes R12's tell easier to see. (5) Give the notepad a bit more room for late-game vote logs.

As Yakuza I had no safe channel for that: a Day PM is visible on the ledger and could be wiretapped, and I couldn't explain why I cared without outing the bond. The rules didn't stop me, but there was no workable option. I also never got to use my Informant data, because I died before the first trial.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked like a rules violation. All were consistent. Oddities in the setup: the Yakuza drew Wiretap plus THREE Informants. That's four passive roles with no blocker, killer or investigator, and the three Informants were fully redundant. Day 1 and Day 2 were 13 near-identical "Agreed, keep it short" messages, so they carried no information. Olivia nominated Carol five times at 2 players alive, where a nomination needs 2 Yes, so each one was sure to fail.
output.suggestions:

- Consider leaving cross-faction Bonded pairs out for Yakuza, or tell both partners whether they share a faction. A Yakuza tied to a random Villager is mostly a hidden liability: the team can't kill or hang that player, and a third-party kill ends you.
- Give dead players a spectator view, or at least their own faction's chat.
- At 2 players alive, warn (or block) nominations that can't reach a majority without the nominee's own vote.
- Nudge Day 1 prompts toward something substantive, so the table doesn't settle into identical messages.

Because the payoff happens during the Day, it's easy to think of it as harmless and forget that you physically go to the target's house. Night 2 was a full-moon night, and eavesdropping on Judy put me at the house the Werewolf rampaged, so I died as a visitor (and the Katana hit me too). A one-line note in the role text ("this is a visit, so Veterans, rampages and Lookouts see or punish it") would help. The "Never blocks wins" lists for Neutrals, read alongside Turncoat and the Hitman's leaving, took several passes before I understood when the game ends.

After I died, I had no spectator view, so I couldn't follow how my will was used.

4) Optionally, tell Bonded players whether their partner shares their faction. As it stands, the Yakuza used my bond to keep me safe (they knew Frank was theirs), while I knew nothing. That imbalance makes the trait a quiet gift to the Yakuza.

answers.bugs_or_oddities:
