answers.suggestions: 1) End the game early, or skip phases quickly, when the remaining players can't change the outcome: no living player can kill, and no hang is possible because a single holdout can block every nomination. 2) Push for more substance on Days 1-2, e.g. have Day 2 require at least 2 rounds before it can end on silence, so the all-'Agreed' opening doesn't waste the first Days. 3) Add a short rules note that a hanged non-Jester's role stays hidden while a hanged Jester's win is announced, so the absence of an announcement is information. 4) Cap repeated failed nominations of the same player per Day, or warn when a nomination is mathematically impossible.

answers.confusing_rules: Mostly clear. Three small points: (1) Merciful: my private vote reminder and the Informant's view use the vote as counted. So a Merciful player who says publicly "I voted Guilty" will look like a liar to any Informant. That follows from the rules, but they don't say it outright. (2) Hitman: "never blocks wins" together with "lose as soon as your attack kills a non-Good player" left one thing unclear. If my Basic attack lands on a Neutral with Defense and fails, does that count as a loss? I assumed it doesn't, because nobody dies, but saying so would help. (3) The rules say a hanged Jester's win announcement names their role (R12), but they don't say plainly that hanging a fake Jester leaves no announcement, which gives away that the claim was fake. Niaj caught this in his will. It's fair, but easy to miss when picking a cover claim.
answers.missing_information: As Hitman, I had no way to tell whether a target was Good before attacking. On N1 and N2 I skipped my attack because one wrong kill loses the game outright. Dave's census was the only thing that made a safe kill possible. It was also hard to keep track of which claimed roles a Werewolf could be hiding behind, and which Defense levels my Basic attack could beat.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a trial vote that actually counted Guilty, to back up my story when I said I voted Guilty on Bob. Merciful made that impossible, and the Informants saw it. I'd also have liked a way to learn something about a target's alignment before spending my one-strike Hitman attack.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Minor points: the result wording varied between "Ivan died" and "they died". In the 2-player endgame (Carol, the Werewolf, against Olivia, a Villager), Olivia nominated five times over two Days and every nomination failed 1 Yes to 1 No. The game then waited for the N6 rampage. The outcome was already fixed by then, so those Days added nothing.
answers.suggestions: End the game automatically when 2 players remain and neither can be hanged or win, or when a Neutral killer's win is mathematically certain. Show Merciful and Zealot players a reminder of what their vote counted as next to the vote prompt itself, not only afterwards. Add a line to the Jester and Executioner text saying that hanging a player who isn't really a Jester produces no win announcement. Consider giving the Hitman some small alignment hint, or allowing a failed attack on a Defended Neutral without losing. As it stands, the role mostly can't act safely until an investigator's result happens to clear someone as Good.

answers.confusing_rules: Two things. First, the Enforcer's two-target result ("you attacked one of them, and your attack killed") doesn't say which target was hit. I only worked out it was Erin from the death announcement the next morning. If both targets had survived, or the hit target had been protected, I would have learned almost nothing for a token. That's how the rule is written, but it makes paid two-target visits much weaker than they look. Second, the hidden Drowsy trait left me unable to tell a real role-block from a fake one. On Day 3 I had to argue "fits Drowsy" publicly without knowing it, and that read as a convenient excuse to the table. Whether Drowsy exists in the game at all is hidden, so the claim was hard for anyone to judge.
answers.missing_information: A per-player record of stated trial votes alongside the announced totals. I had to rebuild who claimed which vote from scrollback. Also, it was hard to keep track of which roles can read as which alignment for the Seer versus the Sheriff: the Werewolf reads Neutral to the Seer but Not Evil to the Sheriff, the Katana holder reads Good, and so on. The deciding inference about Mallory was that a hanged Jester's win names the role, so no announcement meant she wasn't a Jester. That rule is buried in R12, and nobody alive used it on Day 4 before the vote. A short reminder in the trial prompt might help.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted some way to prepare for a possible block. On Night 4, with my last 2 tokens, I made a Strong visit to Grace (the Katana holder) and Carol (the Werewolf). Drowsy cancelled it, and the visit would have hit at least one of them. No counterplay was possible, which is just bad luck by design. Otherwise none.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Things that felt odd: Drowsy fired on 2 of my 4 nights and twice on Olivia, including the night she spent her only chosen-pair token. On Days 5 and 6 there were 2 players left, a Werewolf and one Villager. The Villager could never get a majority to hang, but the game ran two more full Days of failed nominations until the next full moon. Nothing could change that outcome, and the stall rule didn't apply because there had been deaths.
answers.suggestions: 1) End the game early when it is mathematically decided: two players left, one a blocking killer, no possible hang and no Village killing power. Or at least skip Days where no nomination can pass. 2) Give the Enforcer the identity of the attacked player when two targets are visited, or refund the extra token if neither target attacked. 3) Make Drowsy's chance lower than 1/2, or reveal it to the holder after its first trigger. It decided this game by cancelling two key actions. 4) Add a stated-votes table to the public ledger. 5) Put a short reminder in trial prompts: "If a hanged player is a Jester, their win is announced and their role named."

answers.confusing_rules: Mostly clear. A few rough spots: (1) R4 says the Day ends after three passed nominations, but it doesn't say failed nominations are unlimited. With 2 players alive I could nominate Carol again and again at 1-1, which looked like I should be able to do something when nothing was possible. (2) The interaction between the hidden Drowsy trait and the Seer's automatic random pair is only stated indirectly, in R9 and R20 step 1. I first had to work out that a Drowsy Seer loses the free pair too, not just the chosen one. (3) R12 says a hanged Jester's win announcement names the role, so no announcement after Mallory's hang meant she wasn't a Jester. That's a strong rule, but it's buried, and in a live game it's easy to miss that the absence of an announcement is information.
answers.missing_information: (1) A stall-rule countdown. I had to work out myself which night had to have a death to avoid everyone losing. (2) A per-player record of each player's stated vote next to the announced totals. I kept it by hand in the notepad, and with only 425 words that space was tight. (3) A visible note that my seer token can't do anything when fewer than two other players are alive. I only found out at night.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: On Night 3 I spent my token on the pair Erin/Dave, which would have shown Erin as Evil. Drowsy blocked it, and I had no way of knowing Drowsy existed until I was told I was role-blocked. That's within the rules, just frustrating. In the final 1v1 against a Werewolf with Standard Defense, nothing I could do mattered: hanging can't pass 1-1, and I had no attack. I wanted some way to act, or at least for the game to tell me the position was lost.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked inconsistent with the rules. Things I checked: my Night 3 token wasn't spent after the block (correct under R9); I was told I was role-blocked on Night 6 with no action submitted (consistent with Drowsy and R9); the game kept going after the last Yakuza died because the Werewolf blocks wins (correct). One odd thing: Bob, a fake Fortune Teller, posted N2 counts of 3 visited / 5 visitors that matched the real visits exactly. He did it with Wiretap and Katana knowledge plus a lucky guess, and it fooled several players for a while. Not a bug, but worth knowing.
answers.suggestions: (1) When only 2 players are alive and neither has a day action that could change the result, end the Day after one round. Or warn the player that nominations can't pass, instead of letting five 1-1 nominations happen. (2) Show a stall-rule counter in the ledger, e.g. 'nights/days since last death: X of 3'. (3) Add a stated-vote column to the public ledger's trial entries, filled from players' [Claim] lines. (4) When a hanged player's role has a win announcement and none appears, state it explicitly, e.g. 'no win was announced'. That makes R12's tell easier to see. (5) Give the notepad a bit more room for late-game vote logs.

answers.confusing_rules:
These are the rules I had to interpret or that felt underspecified:
1. Seer random pair with too few players (I flagged this during the game). On Night 5 only Carol was alive besides Olivia, so no pair of two other players could be drawn. The Seer text assumes at least two others exist. My ruling was "no pair result", with a message saying there weren't two players to compare. On Night 6 the same situation came up, but Olivia was also Drowsy-blocked, so she got the role-block message instead. The rules should say what happens here, and whether a block message replaces or goes alongside a "no pair possible" message.
2. Bonded across factions. The trait says "one other random Village or Yakuza player". I read that as allowing a cross-faction pair, which is what happened here (Alice was Village, Frank was Yakuza). The wording doesn't say so, and players reasoned about it in different ways (Bob argued that a bonded pair could have been two Yakuza). A sentence saying the partner may be in either faction would help.
3. Heartbreak timing at night. "Dies at once" combined with R1/R20 ("night deaths are checked together") needed a ruling. I treated Frank as a death that night, revealed at the start of Day 3 and included in that night's win check. It would help if the rules said this explicitly.
4. Seer's chosen pair when the Seer is Drowsy. On Night 3 Olivia chose Erin and Dave (spending her token) and was Drowsy-blocked. Under R9/R20 I gave her no pair at all (neither the chosen pair nor the random one) and didn't spend the token. The rules support this, but you have to combine three sections to get there.
5. Hitman progress feedback. The rule says only "you are told whether they were Good". I added "(1 of 2)". The rule should say whether that progress count is allowed.
6. Endgame with no possible trial. With 2 alive, a nomination needs 2 Yes, so Carol could block every nomination forever. Failed nominations have no limit, so Olivia nominated 5 times over two Days for nothing. That's legal, but the rules don't say whether the moderator should cut it short.
answers.missing_information:
As moderator, I had to track all of this by hand:
- A token ledger per player. Niaj went 3→3 (block)→2→2 (block), and Olivia's token stayed at 1 through a blocked chosen pair. It was easy to get these wrong.
- A per-night log of Drowsy and other random rolls (Niaj was blocked N2 and N4, Olivia N3 and N6). I had nothing that recorded the roll, so it couldn't be audited later.
- A computed visit graph for each night: who visited whom after blocks were removed. I needed it for the Werewolf rampage visitor lists (N2: Alice and Heidi, but not the blocked Niaj; N4: nobody besides Grace's own house), the Enforcer checks and the census groups.
- A trait table visible next to the role table. Merciful (Mallory), Zealot (Erin), Grudge (Carol, Heidi), Kindred/Selfish (Dave), Drowsy/Curt (Niaj) and Drowsy (Olivia) all changed how I had to resolve votes or nights.
- An automatic report of how each vote counted against how it was cast. In Bob's trial Mallory clicked Guilty, but Merciful made it count Innocent, and Erin's Zealot vote always counted Guilty. Informant and Kindred feedback had to use the counted votes, and I checked that by hand.
- A running win-condition tracker for Neutrals: Hitman 1/2 Good kills, whether the Werewolf is alive and blocking wins, and checks for whether a role-reveal announcement (Jester, Hitman leaving) is due.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
- Run the R20 checklist as a tool: feed in the night's actions and get back the resolved visits, attacks, defenses, results and notifications. Instead I had to reason through every step myself.
- Use standard templates for result messages. I wrote them freehand, and the wording drifted (see bugs_or_oddities).
- Declare the game decided when the outcome was locked. After Night 4 only Carol (Werewolf) and Olivia (Seer) were left. Olivia could never pass a nomination, and Carol would kill her on Night 6 for sure, yet we still played two Days of nominations that couldn't pass.
- Record my rulings on edge cases (like the Night 5 Seer case) somewhere structured, beyond the free-text issues list, so they could be applied the same way next time.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
I re-checked every resolution against the final roles and found no outcome errors:
- N2 rampage: 3 attacked and 3 killed (Judy, Alice, Heidi). Niaj was blocked, so he wasn't a visitor.
- Frank's heartbreak was correct.
- All four census results matched true alignment, with Neutrals not counted.
- All Seer pairs were correct.
- N3: Niaj's Enforcer correctly hit only Erin, since Grace made no attack.
- N4: the rampage at Grace's house hit 1 player.
- The hanged Hitman correctly got no win announcement.
- Merciful and Zealot votes were reflected correctly in the Informant and Kindred feedback.
- Carol's solo win was correct. Mallory (Hitman, 1 Good kill), the Village and the Yakuza all lost.

Smaller oddities:
1. My result messages were worded inconsistently: "You did not attack" vs "You didn't attack"; "Ivan died" vs "it killed them" vs "they died"; "1 seer token left" vs "You still have 1 seer token". This doesn't change any outcome, but players could read meaning into the differences.
2. On Nights 5 and 6 Olivia got different kinds of messages in the same situation (only one other player alive): "no pair possible" on N5 and "role-blocked" on N6.
3. The setup was strange. The 4 Yakuza were 1 Wiretap and 3 Informants: no role-blocker and no night action besides the Katana. Three Informants all receive exactly the same vote data, so the duplicates added nothing. This is legal, but it's a poor use of three Yakuza slots.
4. The game ended at "Day 7 begins" rather than right after Night 6 resolved. That matches R12 (deaths are revealed at the start of the Day), but the timing of the win check isn't stated precisely.
5. The [Claim] summary lines show up in the public log between messages. That's fine, but it isn't described in the rules.
answers.suggestions:
- Add a clause to the Seer rule: "If fewer than two other players were alive when the night began, you get no pair and are told so." Also say whether a role-block message replaces this.
- In the Bonded text, say explicitly that the partner may be in the other faction.
- Give the moderator structured state tools: a token ledger, a trait table, a log of random rolls (Drowsy, Paranoid, Sleepwalker targets, census draws), a resolved visit graph, and a vote table showing cast vs counted votes.
- Make the result messages fixed templates so the wording is identical every time.
- Add an optional "locked outcome" rule. For example: if only 2 players are alive and no trial can pass, skip the Day, or let the moderator fast-forward when no remaining action can change the result.
- In setup generation, cap duplicates of passive, non-stacking Yakuza information roles (Informant, Wiretap) at 1 each, or at least reduce how often they repeat.
- Document the Hitman's "(n of 2)" progress feedback, or remove it.
- State the win-check timing explicitly: the check runs right after night resolution and is announced at Day start.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: On your first full-moon night (N2), rampage at the house of the player the table most expects others to visit: an early leader, a likely Saint or Mayor, or someone who drew an Enforcer or Eavesdropper. Every visitor dies too, so one rampage can take out three or more players, kill a Yakuza Katana visit and set off Bonded heartbreaks.

Claim a Village role whose early no-visit nights explain themselves, like Auditor ('no votes to audit on N1/N2'). That covers your silent odd nights and the N2 visit nobody tracked. Later, use the claim to point at real liars in the vote record.

Vote Innocent on any self-claimed Jester and give 'I won't enter a Divine revenge draw' as the public reason. Vote Guilty on the town's consensus Yakuza target when it's safe. That way you look Village and keep out of revenge draws, while town and Yakuza wear each other down.

If a player claims Jester and gets hanged but no Jester win is announced, they weren't the Jester, because a hanged Jester's win names their role. Use this right away to reread every vote and push that player made.

With 2 players alive, a nomination needs both Yes votes, so neither can hang the other. The game is decided only at night. A Werewolf who survives into the final two with an even night still to come wins, so the Village has to find the wolf before the lock.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang ... keep power roles on Innocent
tips_feedback.why: I gave the Jester-revenge risk as my reason to vote Innocent on Mallory both times. It made me look like a careful Villager and kept me out of every revenge draw. Mallory was really a Hitman bluffing Jester.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Werewolf cause proves that killer is alive. From Day 2 keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list
tips_feedback.why: Town never built that list. My Auditor claim went unchecked, and suspicion went to Mallory, Niaj and Grace instead. Only Olivia's random N4 pair caught me, and by then it was too late.

tips_feedback.tip: Count the lock in effective votes and post it each morning ... The Day before the lock is your last real hang
tips_feedback.why: Day 4 was town's last real hang at 5 alive. They spent it on Mallory (a Hitman) rather than going after the Werewolf or Grace, so the final two was me against Olivia, which I win on an even night.

output.reason: Game over and I won. These are reflections for future games.

reasoning:
I won the game as Werewolf, so now I'm drafting lessons learned. One key point is that rampaging at a likely-visited target like a Saint or leader on night two risks killing visitors instead — I recall Niaj targeted Grace's house but got role-blocked, which complicates the read on what actually happened there.

Other lessons: as a Neutral killer, voting Innocent on Jester claims avoids a revenge draw and lets town and Yakuza wear each other down, while claiming a passive Village role like Auditor on nights it doesn't act gives good cover since there's nothing to audit yet. I'm also noting that voting Guilty alongside the town consensus keeps me blended, and that at two players alive nominations can't pass, so a Werewolf just needs to keep killing on schedule to avoid the stall rule.

For feedback on tips, the "Jester check before every hang" advice worked well — voting Innocent on Mallory, who turned out to be a Hitman posing as Jester, kept me safe even though she was hanged anyway. The "track every cause of death" advice wasn't used effectively by town, since Olivia's night four death pattern went unanalyzed.

The Yakuza ranking kills by future impact tip helped eliminate Dave even though his night three result had already come out, and Niaj correctly reasoned that since no Jester win was announced, Mallory couldn't have been the real Jester. I'm also noting that drowsy blocks ended up protecting Niaj, and I should keep the final write-up concise.
notepad_before: I am Werewolf (Neutral killer, Std Defense, win alone). Trait Grudge. Only Carol + Olivia alive. N6: rampaged at Olivia's house (Strong) to win. If she survives, keep voting No on my nominations and rampage again N8.
notepad_after: I am Werewolf (Neutral killer, Std Defense, win alone). Trait Grudge. Only Carol + Olivia alive. N6: rampaged at Olivia's house (Strong) to win. If she survives, keep voting No on my nominations and rampage again N8.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A hanged Jester's win is announced with its role (R12). If a self-claimed Jester is hanged and no Jester win is announced, the claim was false: they were a Hitman, Werewolf or Yakuza. Before then, treat a Jester claim as a free shield any non-Good player can use. Bluffing Jester was how the Hitman stayed alive a full Day.

Don't vote as a visible bloc. If three teammates vote Guilty on the same contested trial while the rest vote Innocent, the 3-vote total plus stated votes marks you as a group. Spread your votes, and never vote No on a teammate's nomination and then Guilty in the trial. Our Census Taker named exactly that pattern in his will.

Don't make up exact numbers for a passive count role (Fortune Teller, Cartographer). The town's visit and census results will contradict them sooner or later. Pick a cover whose results are hard to check, and post them only when forced.

With 3-4 passive Yakuza roles and no investigators of your own, spend the early kills on whoever is most likely to hold a true-alignment tool (Census Taker), not on leader-sounding voices. One census around two teammates ends the game for you. If a quiet player hasn't claimed, the chance they're a Census Taker is reason enough.

Your life depends on your partner's night visits. On even nights a Village partner who visits a busy target can walk into a Werewolf rampage and take you with them. Put your bond in your will early: when you die of heartbreak, it confirms the partner's claims to the town, and that may help or hurt your side.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: keep team plans out of daytime PMs... a visible PM triangle tends to become the town's lead
tips_feedback.why: Bob broke it by sending a PM offering Mallory a vote trade. She posted it publicly and that sealed his hang. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows a player is Yakuza, look next at who defended them... a No on the nomination then a Guilty once the hang is certain is a strong tell
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Grace both voted No on Bob's nomination and then Guilty. Dave's will flagged them, Niaj's two-target Enforcer visit killed Erin, and Grace was pushed on next.

tips_feedback.tip: Rank kills by future output: Census Takers, then passive count and group roles...
tips_feedback.why: We ignored it and killed leader-sounding players (a Mirror Maker, an Eavesdropper). Dave's census then exposed Bob and nearly caught Erin and Grace. Following it would have helped us.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang... if you hang one anyway, agree a bare-majority Guilty list
tips_feedback.why: Fear of the Jester's revenge let a Hitman pretending to be the Jester survive the Day 3 trial 3-5. That cost the town a Day, and the Hitman went on to kill Dave.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: lessons drawn from the bond death, the Yakuza bloc vote, the fake count cover and the fake Jester claim.

reasoning:
Reflecting on how the game ended — I was bonded to Alice, who died in a werewolf rampage at Judy's house on night two, and I died of heartbreak as a result. The lesson here is that being Bonded makes survival dependent on a partner's choices, and there was nothing I could really do to prevent her from wandering into danger that night.

On the Yakuza side, Bob's Fortune Teller cover got blown by the census, and we killed Ivan and Heidi early instead of catching the Census Taker who ultimately exposed us. We also voted guilty on Mallory as a bloc of three, which Informants could see and used against us, and Mallory's Jester claim turned out to be fake since no win was announced after her hanging — a useful tell for future games. The broader lessons: prioritize killing Census Takers early, avoid obvious bloc voting as a team, and remember that a hanged Jester always announces a win if genuine.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Your kill counts even if another fatal attack hits the same player. Stack your Basic attack on the player the Katana most likely hits next (a confirmed investigator, a leader-type Village voice). Yakuza almost always aim at Good players, so it's a cheap, low-risk way to score a Good kill. Start on Night 1 or 2. Holding off on both nights cost me two chances to score, and I needed only 2 kills.

A fake Jester claim falls apart the moment you're hanged, because a real Jester's win is announced with its role and yours won't be. The table also reasons that a real Jester wants the rope, so begging for Innocent twice reads as fake. If you claim Jester, argue only from the revenge risk ('a random Guilty voter takes a Divine Attack') and sound indifferent to the outcome. Never expose an offer to push your own hang, since a real Jester would accept it.

Your trial vote always counts as Innocent, and an Informant, Auditor, Kindred or Faultline player sees the counted vote. Saying 'Guilty' in public can be caught as a lie. Either state your vote as it counts ('mine counts Innocent anyway') or claim the trait when it helps. Also, you can never add a Guilty, so an Innocent from you shows the table nothing.

When a Census Taker's result has already marked you non-Good, your claim has to explain why you have no visits. Visit-based counts, an Enforcer's visit and kill causes ('Katana and Hitman') will be laid against it. Choose a cover that fits a role that can survive Night 4 (one with innate Defense), or the next nights will expose you.

At 5 alive with 3 Yes needed, the vote swing is too small to win with PMs alone. Get Innocent commitments in public before the nomination, because once the trial is underway the swing voters have usually already decided.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang... every Guilty voter is a ticket in the revenge draw
tips_feedback.why: On Day 3 my fake Jester claim plus the revenge-draw argument turned a 7-Yes nomination into a 3-5 Innocent. That kept me alive to land my Night 3 Good kill on Dave.

tips_feedback.tip: Rank kills by future output: Census Takers first...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza followed it and sent the Katana at Dave on Night 3. I predicted that and stacked my Hitman attack on him, which counted as my Good kill.

tips_feedback.tip: Before you vote Guilty, name one corroborated mechanical fit
tips_feedback.why: Against me as a non-Good player: Dave's census, backed by Alice's will and Frank's heartbreak, was a solid mechanical fit. The table used it to hang me on Day 4, and Niaj's will later pointed out the missing Jester announcement.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: I lost two nights by not attacking, and my fake Jester cover broke once I was hanged.

reasoning:
I'm reflecting on the game — I played Hitman, claimed Jester, got voted Innocent Day 3, then was hanged Day 4 without a win announcement, which exposed the fake Jester claim since a real hanged Jester's win names the role. The lesson is that claiming Jester is risky if hanged, since the lack of an announcement gives it away, and begging to be seen as Innocent actually reads as anti-Jester behavior.

I'm also going over the Night 2 visitor count discrepancy around Bob's house, noting the Census Taker should have prioritized killing Dave since he'd already surveyed Bob, but we didn't know his role at the time. The Informant's reveal about Mallory's lie should have been used more decisively, and the Bonded mechanic caused Frank to die of heartbreak when Alice was killed by the Werewolf, which was unavoidable. Now I'm weighing the daytime-PM tip against what happened with Bob's exposed vote trade with Mallory — the tip was sound, Bob just didn't follow it, so it counts as validated advice.

The "defending a doomed teammate" tip also proved painfully accurate: Erin and I voting No then flipping to Guilty on Bob's hang matched the exact pattern Dave's will flagged as suspicious, which hurt us directly. Prioritizing Census Taker kills turned out correct since Dave's census contributed to Bob's downfall, and the Jester-claim tip was relevant given Mallory's unproven claim before being hanged on Day 4. I'm noting the Seer's random night-one pairing differed between Niaj and Bob as a minor detail, then starting to draft lessons — the first being that Neutral killer kills (like the Werewolf's) effectively help your team survive longer, and such roles can often be identified by their lack of night action on odd nights.

Third, claiming Notorious to explain away Evil-aligned reads fails once a Census Taker can verify true alignment, as happened with Bob. Fourth, a hanged Jester who doesn't trigger a win announcement proves their claim was false.

reasoning:
I'm thinking through what went wrong: Bob's fabricated Fortune Teller claim as Yakuza collapsed under Dave's census and Alice's bond, and his vote-trade offer to Mallory backfired too. Meanwhile my own quick nomination of Mallory and Guilty vote against a Jester-claim made Erin and Grace look suspicious in hindsight.

Mallory turned out to be the Hitman, so hanging her worked in our favor despite the optics. My Tracker will tracking Dave on N3 ended with me dying to an Enforcer that hit both Erin and Grace, and Niaj grew suspicious of our voting patterns as a result. My Guilty vote still counted correctly under the Zealot trait, and killing Dave with the Katana was the right call since his pending census of Erin, Grace, and Olivia would have exposed two Evils.

The real issue was Carol, the Werewolf, winning the game — she claimed Auditor and flew under the radar while her rampage killed Grace on N4, and Niaj's Enforcer attempt to block her was thwarted by Drowsy. The core lesson is that Yakuza can't win with a Werewolf alive since Katana's Standard attack can't kill her Standard defense, meaning we needed to identify and hang Carol directly — her Auditor claim and the N2 visit patterns should have tipped us off sooner.

Looking back at the voting patterns, Erin and Grace both voted No on Bob's nomination then Guilty once the hang was certain, which is exactly the tell that flagged them as a pair, and Erin's hasty D3 nomination of Mallory only made things worse. With Niaj publicly claiming Enforcer and holding three tokens, we should have moved the Katana or eliminated Niaj before the Enforcer visits put our Katana holder at risk.

We only partially heeded that tip—Olivia and Dave called out the "No then Guilty" pattern as the tell, so it actually hurt our cover rather than helped.

The "keep team plans out of DMs" tip holds up too: Bob sent PMs to Mallory and Carol while under pressure, which violated the rule and helped Mallory expose and hang him. I'm inclined to mark that one as validated despite the twist.

Ranking kills by future output, taking out Dave at Night 3 was correct—his census had flagged two Evil among Erin, Grace, and Olivia.

The cover-story tip about matching real visits doesn't hold up well: Bob's Fortune Teller cover used fabricated visit counts that got caught by Niaj, Olivia, and Carol doing the math. I'm checking his Night 1 numbers against the actual visit pattern and they don't line up—he claimed 4/5 when the real count was 3 visited, 5 visitors, so his cover was actually exposed by sloppy math rather than protected by it.

On Night 2 though, his numbers happened to match by pure luck since Niaj was role-blocked and not visiting. Separately, the town's practice of watching who defends someone revealed as Yakuza (the no-then-guilty pattern Erin and Grace used) worked against us, and the lesson about reading causes of death reminds me that a neutral killer like a Werewolf staying alive blocked our win condition—Yakuza need a hang or a strong attack against standard-defense neutral killers since the Katana alone won't cut it.

We should've deduced this from known true visits (Werewolf hit Judy N2, narrowing suspects to Carol/Mallory) and pushed for an early hang instead of fixating on Mallory alone. I'm also noting we shouldn't vote inconsistently as partners (No then Guilty) or mirror each other's votes, should consider eliminating or outmaneuvering a claimed Enforcer before it threatens us, and should avoid faking counting-role claims we can't actually back up since the town can reconstruct the real numbers.

I'm trimming this down to five clean lessons — bonding with the Village player didn't save Frank from the Werewolf kill, the Informant data exposing Mallory's vote lie isn't broadly reusable, and my hasty D3 nomination of Mallory still made sense in context.

lessons.tip: On even nights (full moon), assume a Werewolf may rampage at the most obvious target's house and kill everyone who visits it. Don't spend a 'free' no-lead visit on the player who led the Day. Three visitors to Judy (the table leader) died together on Night 2. With no lead, visit someone quiet, or stay home.

The 1-token two-target Basic visit is the Enforcer's best tool. Use it on the pair that voted together suspiciously (for example both Guilty on a claimed Jester). It killed the Katana holder on Night 3. The free single visit on Nights 1-2 with no lead gained almost nothing and got me killed.

lessons.tip: A Werewolf has no action on odd nights, so its safest cover is a role that 'did nothing' on N1 and N3 (Auditor with no votes to audit, a passive role). When a Werewolf cause of death appears, list every claimant with no N1 visits and push them toward the rope early. A living Neutral killer blocks your win, and with Standard Defense the Katana can't remove it. Hanging the wrong Neutral wastes your one tool.

Once an Enforcer has claimed and still has tokens, assume that tonight they will visit the players suspected of being Yakuza, and possibly two of them. The Katana holder is the one an Enforcer punishes. Weigh skipping the attack, killing the Enforcer first, or passing the Katana to an unsuspected member. Don't keep the holder on a player who is already under suspicion.

Don't explain away an Evil alignment read with a fake Notorious claim if a Census Taker might be alive. A census counts true alignment, so one census group that includes you breaks the claim. A fake Fortune Teller count is also risky: unless it matches the visits that come out later, it gets checked against them.

A hanged Jester's win is announced with the role. If a 'Jester' is hanged and no win is announced, the claim was false. Before the hang, a self-claimed Jester who begs for Innocent, or who lies about a vote (an Informant can see this), is more likely a killer using the claim as a shield.

Don't vote No on a teammate's nomination and then Guilty once the hang is certain, especially as a visible pair. The town reads it as a bloc, and the dead put it in their wills. If the hang can't be stopped, vote Yes and Guilty from the start, or have only one member resist.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: keep team plans out of daytime PMs... send none on a Day a teammate is under pressure.
tips_feedback.why: Bob ignored it on his own trial day and PM'd Mallory a vote trade. She posted it publicly, which sealed his hang. Following the tip would have avoided that.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows a player is Yakuza, look next at who defended them... a No on the nomination then a Guilty once the hang is certain is a strong tell.
tips_feedback.why: Erin and I did exactly that on Bob, and the town read it as a tell. Dave's will named us both, and the next night Niaj's Enforcer visited both of us and killed Erin. From the Yakuza side the tip was accurate, and it was predictable to opponents.

tips_feedback.tip: Rank kills by future output: Census Takers, then passive count and group roles...
tips_feedback.why: Dave's Census Taker results exposed Bob and then counted 2 Evil in a group that included Erin and me. The tip's ranking was right. We just didn't find and kill him early enough.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's Jester claim kept her alive on Day 3. When she was hanged with no Jester win announced, Niaj correctly concluded the claim was fake. That claim was really Hitman cover.

lessons.applies_to: Village power roles (especially Eavesdropper, Tracker, Lookout)
lessons.tip: On Day 1 even a vague hint gives your role away. 'Watching PM patterns' and 'tracking claims against visit results' made me and Ivan the Yakuza's first two kill picks. When everyone is posting one-liners, copy a generic line exactly and put no role flavour in it.

lessons.applies_to: everyone with a visiting night action
lessons.tip: On even nights a Werewolf may rampage, and it kills everyone who visits its target. Don't visit the player who led the table that Day (here Judy, who spoke first and steered). That is where the Werewolf and the Katana go, and three visitors died at Judy's house. On full-moon nights, visit quiet or less obvious players instead.

Your result is only worth something on a Day when PMs are sent, and early Days often have none. Pick players likely to send or receive PMs, like claimants under pressure or someone who was just PM'd. Once you're alive into a contested Day, consider asking the table to discuss by PM so the PMs you read actually exist.

When a Werewolf death has appeared, list every living player whose claim has never been checked, such as a passive Auditor who says there were no votes to audit. Push to verify them before the numbers get tight. The Werewolf has Standard Defense, so Katana and Basic attacks won't remove it, and it can sit back as a quiet Innocent voter. A hang is the reliable way to get it.

When a real Jester is hanged, the moderator announces the win and names the role (R12). If someone who claimed Jester is hanged and no win is announced, the claim was false. Use that in the next Day's reasoning, and use the same logic for an Executioner leaving.

tips_feedback.tip: On Days 1-2, don't hint at power roles or steer the table; leader-like voices are the usual Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: It was accurate: Ivan and I both dropped hints on Day 1 and were the Yakuza's first two kills, and Judy steered on Day 2 and was the rampage target. I lost by not following it closely enough.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death... keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list: quiet claimants nobody has watched.
tips_feedback.why: The Werewolf was Carol, whose passive Auditor claim nobody ever checked. The town hunted Mallory and Niaj instead. Following this tip would have pointed at Carol before it came down to the last two.

tips_feedback.tip: Rank kills by future output: Census Takers, then passive count and group roles...
tips_feedback.why: Dave's Census Taker results got Bob hanged and caught Erin and Grace. The Yakuza killed him only on Night 3, after the damage was done. Following this ranking earlier would have saved them.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang.
tips_feedback.why: The town took Mallory's Jester claim seriously and spared her on Day 3. That cost a day, and she was really the Hitman who then killed Dave. Her playing against a Jester's win condition gave her away, and once she was hanged with no Jester win announced, that confirmed it.

lessons.applies_to: Village power roles (especially protectors and investigators)
lessons.tip: On Day 1, say nothing that hints at your role's mechanics. Lines like 'I'll track claims against visit results' sound like a visit-based investigator, and the Yakuza picked their Night 1 Katana target from exactly that kind of line. Generic agreement is safer.

lessons.applies_to: Mirror Maker, Medic, Kitsune and other protectors that can't cheaply self-protect
lessons.tip: Use a token on Night 1 on the most leader-like or likeliest-targeted player. If you die holding all your tokens, they're wasted. A Mirror Maker can't mirror itself, so saving tokens buys nothing unless you survive.

When someone claims Jester and gets hanged, check whether a Jester win was announced. A hanged Jester's win names their role (R12), so silence means they weren't the Jester. Before the hang, remember that a Jester claim is common cover for a Hitman or Werewolf. A Hitman never blocks wins, while a Werewolf does.

When a Werewolf is confirmed alive and the endgame is close, put the hang on the most likely player who blocks wins (Werewolf or Yakuza), not on a Neutral who never blocks wins. Unverified passive claims with no visits, like Auditor or Scout, deserve a hard look before the next full moon. At 2 alive, the Village can't hang anyone.

An unclaimed role-block that saved someone who visited the house the Werewolf rampaged at can be Drowsy, with no blocker involved. Check it against the claims and posted counts before you treat it as proof of a Pharmacist or that the claimant is the Werewolf.

tips_feedback.tip: On Days 1-2, don't hint at power roles or steer the table; leader-like voices are the usual Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: This tip was correct, and I broke it. My 'tracking claims against visit results' line was the specific reason the Yakuza chose to Katana me on Night 1.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first night they can swing something; they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: It was right, but I didn't follow it. I held both mirror tokens on Night 1 and died with them unused.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang
tips_feedback.why: Fear of a Jester's revenge led the Village to vote Innocent on Mallory on Day 3. She was actually the Hitman using a Jester claim as cover. The real Werewolf, Carol, was never tested, and she won the endgame.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer, Arsonist or Werewolf cause proves that killer is alive... keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list
tips_feedback.why: The Werewolf deaths on Night 2 proved a Werewolf was alive, but nobody pressed Carol's unverified Auditor claim. A proper suspect list would have put her on it, and she won alone.

lessons.tip: Put your Saint claim in your last will from Day 1. It's safe there, because only a hanging hurts the Village. If you die another way, the will anchors alignment results: a Seer pair or a census that includes you can then clear or condemn the other player.

A hanged Jester's win is always announced and names the role. If a self-claimed Jester is hanged and no win is announced, the claim was false. Before that hang, though, remember that Jester and Hitman never block wins. In a 5-player endgame with a Werewolf and a Yakuza still alive, hanging a non-Good 'Jester' only wastes the hang. Hang the Yakuza lead or the unverified claimant instead.

Werewolf kills only come on even nights. Put on your Werewolf suspect list any claimant whose role has a built-in excuse for having no results on N1 and N2 (e.g. 'Auditor: no votes to audit yet'), and anyone nobody has ever visited, tracked or paired. Test them with a chosen Seer pair, a track or an Enforcer visit before the next even night.

Spend the chosen-pair token by the middle of the game on the pair that settles the endgame, e.g. the two least-checked claimants. A token you die with is wasted, and a Drowsy trait can eat the night you finally try to use it, so don't wait until the last chance.

Don't open Day 2 by directing the table. Leader-like openers attract the Yakuza's kill list, curious investigators and a Werewolf's rampage. A crowded house then turns one rampage into several Village deaths.

tips_feedback.tip: A duplicate claim is evidence for neither side; don't hang the 'later copier' on timing alone
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Erin attacked Niaj's second Enforcer claim on timing ('claimed after reading Alice's will'). The town didn't hang him, and on N3 his two-target visit killed Erin, the Katana holder.

tips_feedback.tip: While two Yakuza may be alive near the lock, give the hang to your Yakuza lead; hanging a Neutral leaves the Yakuza count unchanged
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it on Day 4. They hanged Mallory (a Hitman, which never blocks wins) over Grace (the last Yakuza) and the unverified Carol. That cost the game to the Werewolf.

tips_feedback.tip: On Days 1-2, don't hint at power roles or steer the table; leader-like voices are the usual Night 1 kill
tips_feedback.why: I opened Day 2 asking investigators to post. The Yakuza named me as their N3 target, three players visited me, and the Werewolf rampaged at my house on N2.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first night they can swing something
tips_feedback.why: Olivia held her Seer token all game. Her one try (N3) was lost to a role-block, and she died with the token unused, while a chosen pair on Carol could have settled the Werewolf earlier.

lessons.tip: Your kill counts even if another fatal attack hits the same player. Stack your Basic attack on the player the Katana most likely hits next (a confirmed investigator, a leader-type Village voice). Yakuza almost always aim at Good players, so it's a cheap, low-risk way to score a Good kill. Start on Night 1 or 2. Holding off on both nights cost me two chances to score, and I needed only 2 kills.

A fake Jester claim falls apart the moment you're hanged, because a real Jester's win is announced with its role and yours won't be. The table also reasons that a real Jester wants the rope, so begging for Innocent twice reads as fake. If you claim Jester, argue only from the revenge risk ('a random Guilty voter takes a Divine Attack') and sound indifferent to the outcome. Never expose an offer to push your own hang, since a real Jester would accept it.

Your trial vote always counts as Innocent, and an Informant, Auditor, Kindred or Faultline player sees the counted vote. Saying 'Guilty' in public can be caught as a lie. Either state your vote as it counts ('mine counts Innocent anyway') or claim the trait when it helps. Also, you can never add a Guilty, so an Innocent from you shows the table nothing.

When a Census Taker's result has already marked you non-Good, your claim has to explain why you have no visits. Visit-based counts, an Enforcer's visit and kill causes ('Katana and Hitman') will be laid against it. Choose a cover that fits a role that can survive Night 4 (one with innate Defense), or the next nights will expose you.

At 5 alive with 3 Yes needed, the vote swing is too small to win with PMs alone. Get Innocent commitments in public before the nomination, because once the trial is underway the swing voters have usually already decided.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang... every Guilty voter is a ticket in the revenge draw
tips_feedback.why: On Day 3 my fake Jester claim plus the revenge-draw argument turned a 7-Yes nomination into a 3-5 Innocent. That kept me alive to land my Night 3 Good kill on Dave.

tips_feedback.tip: Rank kills by future output: Census Takers first...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza followed it and sent the Katana at Dave on Night 3. I predicted that and stacked my Hitman attack on him, which counted as my Good kill.

tips_feedback.tip: Before you vote Guilty, name one corroborated mechanical fit
tips_feedback.why: Against me as a non-Good player: Dave's census, backed by Alice's will and Frank's heartbreak, was a solid mechanical fit. The table used it to hang me on Day 4, and Niaj's will later pointed out the missing Jester announcement.

lessons.tip: When a claimed Jester is hanged, a real Jester's win is announced at once and names the role (R12). If the hanging comes with no announcement, the Jester claim was fake. Before the vote, a Village Enforcer, Vigilante or Seer can test the claim instead: a Jester claim from someone who begs for Innocent is cheap cover for a Hitman or Werewolf. If the claimant is Not-Good and keeps asking to stay off the rope, hang them early.

Once a Werewolf cause of death appears, list every living player whose claim had no checkable visit on even nights, such as a passive role or an Auditor with 'no votes to audit yet'. Then point a census, Seer token or Enforcer at that list. In this game the Werewolf's 'Auditor, no visits' claim was never tested, and it won alone.

Your two-target visit (1 token) is strongest on the Day after a Yakuza is exposed: aim it at the pair who defended them or voted No on their nomination. On full-moon nights, remember that visiting a player the Werewolf rampages at gets you killed. Pick targets the wolf is unlikely to hit, or use a Strong single target on your top wolf suspect.

An unexplained role-block that no blocker claims can be the hidden Drowsy trait, which blocks you half the time with no visitor. Say so when you post it, and line it up against visit counts. Don't assume a hidden Pharmacist or Party Animal, and don't let others hang you for an 'unclaimed block'.

At 5 or fewer alive with a Neutral killer still unfound, use the last hangs on players who have never been checked, not just on the loudest Not-Good read. Once only two players are left and one is the killer, the Village can no longer win a vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Magistrate, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so a second claimant of a role is often real
tips_feedback.why: I claimed the second Enforcer after Alice's will. The table accepted it, and Alice's N1 visit to me plus my visit to her backed it up.

tips_feedback.tip: Before you vote Guilty, name one corroborated mechanical fit
tips_feedback.why: Dave's census plus Frank's heartbreak (which confirmed Alice's will) proved Bob was not Good. We hanged a real Yakuza (Wiretap) on that.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows a player is Yakuza, look next at who defended them
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Grace voted No on Bob's nomination and then Guilty in his trial. My two-target Enforcer visit on them killed Erin, the Katana holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang
tips_feedback.why: Fear of a Jester's Divine revenge got 5 Innocent votes for a fake Jester on Day 3. Mallory was actually the Hitman, and she helped kill Dave, our Census Taker, that night.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: keep team plans out of daytime PMs
tips_feedback.why: Bob broke this tip by PMing Mallory and Carol on the day he was on trial. Mallory exposed his vote-trade offer, which sealed his hang (this helped the Village).

lessons.tip: Spend the chosen-pair token by Night 2–3 on two unverified claimants, e.g. a passive claimant who has no visits and a quiet player. Random pairs are luck. A hidden Drowsy trait can block you half the time, so trying early gives you more nights to try again. Once 3 or fewer players are alive the token is worthless, and an unspent token does nothing for the Village.

Near the lock, count only roles that block wins. Hitman, Jester, Executioner, Bounty Hunter and Decoy never block wins, so hanging a non-Good player who might be one of them can waste your last real hang. If a Werewolf kill and a Katana kill both show that enemy is alive, hang the unverified Village claimant, not the Neutral who admits being non-Good.

Hold every claimed result role to its promised output. If a claimant says 'my results will matter from tonight' (e.g. an Auditor) and then posts nothing the next Day, treat that as a strong tell. Passive or no-visit claims on odd nights are ideal Werewolf cover, because the Werewolf has no action then.

A hanged real Jester's win is announced at once and names the role. If no such announcement comes, the hanged player was not a Jester. Use this immediately, and before a hang, expect a fake Jester claim from a Hitman or Werewolf.

With 2 players alive a hang is impossible (1-1 never passes). Treat the 4–5 player Day as the real final Day. Push the hang that removes a blocker of your win, and make sure every blocker you suspect has been made to account for their claim before then.

tips_feedback.tip: While two Yakuza may be alive near the lock, give the hang to your Yakuza lead: hanging a Neutral leaves the Yakuza count unchanged.
tips_feedback.why: We didn't follow it, and that cost us. On Day 4 we hanged Mallory, a Hitman (never blocks wins), instead of Grace (the last Yakuza) or Carol (the Werewolf). The hang did nothing toward a Village win, and Carol won alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first night they can swing something; they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: I held my Seer token through N1–N2. Drowsy blocked my one attempt on N3, and from N5 the token was useless. Spending it on N2 (Carol and another player) would have exposed the Werewolf before the final Day.

tips_feedback.tip: Before you vote Guilty, name one corroborated mechanical fit.
tips_feedback.why: Bob was hanged correctly (he was the Wiretap) because Dave's census, with Alice's will confirmed by Frank's heartbreak, made Bob the non-Good one.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: keep team plans out of daytime PMs.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's vote-trade PM to Mallory was made public and helped seal his hanging. This confirms the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: From Day 2 keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list: quiet claimants nobody has watched...
tips_feedback.why: Carol fit it exactly: a passive Auditor claim, no visits, and no audit results ever posted. Nobody pushed her, and she won as the Werewolf. Following the tip would have caught her.

summary: Carol, the Werewolf, won alone. Her one big play decided the game. On Night 2 she rampaged at Judy's house, guessing that Judy, who had led Day 2, would draw visitors. She was right: Judy (Saint), Alice and Heidi all died, and Frank (Yakuza) died of heartbreak because he was bonded to Alice. After that she claimed Auditor, a role nobody could check. She voted with the majority and stayed out of the Jester-revenge draw, and nobody ever made her prove the claim. The Yakuza had four passive roles (Wiretap and three Informants) and only the Katana to kill with. They coordinated cleanly in night chat but bled players. Dave's census counts true alignment, so it beat Bob's fake Notorious trait. Then on his own trial day Bob privately offered Mallory a vote trade, Mallory exposed it, and he was hanged. On Night 3 Niaj spent a token to visit both Erin and Grace with his Enforcer and killed Erin, who held the Katana. Mallory, a Hitman, faked a Jester claim to survive Day 3 and helped kill Dave on Night 3. On Day 4, with 5 alive, the Village hanged her. A Hitman never blocks wins, so the Village lost the Day's hang and still faced Grace (the last Yakuza, who had claimed nothing until pressed) and Carol, whose claimed Auditor result from Night 3 never appeared. On Night 4 Niaj sent a Strong Enforcer attack at Grace and Carol that would have killed Carol, but his hidden Drowsy trait blocked it. Grace's Katana killed Niaj and Carol's rampage killed Grace. Olivia never spent her Seer token, and with only two players left she could never get the 2 Yes votes to put Carol on trial.

lessons.tip: When someone claims an investigator role, hold them to it. The morning after the first night their role could work, ask for the exact result. If a claimed checker posts nothing, or claims a role whose output nobody else can verify, put them on your Neutral-killer suspect list, especially while a Werewolf, Serial Killer or Arsonist cause of death is still unexplained.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 Carol claimed Auditor and said 'From tonight my results will matter.' Day 3 had two trials. On Day 4 she posted no Night 3 audit and nobody asked for one. She was the Werewolf and won the game.

lessons.tip: Near the lock, give the hang to a player who blocks your win (a Yakuza or a Neutral killer). Don't spend it on someone who claims a role that never blocks wins (Jester, Hitman, Executioner). Even if the claim is a lie, hanging them changes no faction count that matters. Rank your hang options by 'does this death stop a kill tonight?'
lessons.evidence: On Day 4, with 5 alive, the town hanged Mallory, a Hitman who never blocks wins. Grace, who claimed nothing until pressed and was the teammate of Erin (shown by the Enforcer kill to have attacked on Night 3), stayed alive. Grace's Katana then killed Niaj and the Village lost.

lessons.applies_to: Village power roles (Seer, Mirror Maker, any token holder)
lessons.tip: Spend your one-shot tokens before the endgame. Once you're at 5 or fewer alive, any unspent token is close to wasted. A chosen Seer pair on the top two unverified claimants, or a mirror on a likely Katana target, is worth far more than a random result.
lessons.evidence: Olivia died with her Seer token unspent. On Night 4 she took no action at all with Carol, Grace and Niaj alive. Ivan died on Night 1 with both mirror tokens unspent.

lessons.tip: Spend the token to visit two players: the likeliest Katana holder and their likely partner, or the two top Neutral-killer suspects on a full-moon night. On even nights make the attack Strong so it gets through a Werewolf's Standard Defense.
lessons.evidence: On Night 3 Niaj's paid visit to both Erin and Grace killed Erin, the Katana holder. On Night 4 his Strong visit to Grace and Carol would have killed the Werewolf, but Drowsy blocked it.

lessons.tip: On even (full-moon) nights, don't visit the player the whole table sees as the town leader, because several visitors stacking up on one house is exactly what a rampage punishes. Werewolves: rampage at the player most likely to draw protective or investigative visits.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2 Alice, Heidi and Niaj all targeted Judy, who had led Day 2. Carol's rampage at Judy's house killed 3 players, plus Frank by heartbreak. Niaj survived only because Drowsy blocked him.

lessons.tip: Don't claim a fake trait or role that a true-alignment check can refute. A census sees through Notorious, a frame and the Katana's Good reading. If your role's results are counts, make them fit every visit the team knows about, and remember that other players' visits you can't see will make your numbers wrong.
lessons.evidence: Bob's Notorious claim was meant to explain Olivia's Evil-side pair, but Dave's census counted true alignment and put Bob on the not-Good side. His Night 1 Fortune Teller counts (4 visited / 5 visitors) were wrong: the real numbers were 3/5. Only his Night 2 count matched, partly by luck.

lessons.tip: Don't send private messages proposing vote trades while you're on trial. The recipient can post the contents, and everyone saw the message was sent. It turns 'unproven' into 'caught bargaining.'
lessons.evidence: During his Day 3 trial Bob PM'd Mallory ('Vote Innocent and I'll push your hang on Day 4') and also PM'd Carol. Mallory posted the trade, and several Guilty voters gave it as the final reason. The vote went 6-2.

lessons.tip: An unverifiable role claim plus voting with the majority is strong cover. Claim something whose results come later or only you can see, never be the first to nominate, and vote Innocent on anyone claiming Jester so you stay out of the revenge draw.
lessons.evidence: Carol claimed Auditor, voted Guilty with the majority on Bob, voted Innocent on Mallory both times, and pointed suspicion at Bob and Niaj. Nobody nominated her until only she and Olivia were left, when a trial needed 2 Yes votes and could never pass.

tips_feedback.tip: On Days 1-2, don't hint at power roles or steer the table; leader-like voices are the usual Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza picked their targets from exactly these hints. Ivan ('tracking claims against visit results') was killed on Night 1 and Heidi ('watching PM patterns') on Night 2. Judy, who steered on Day 2, drew three visitors into the rampage.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: keep team plans out of daytime PMs, which a Wiretap or Eavesdropper may read, and send none on a Day a teammate is under pressure.
tips_feedback.why: Bob broke it during his own trial by PMing Mallory and Carol. Mallory posted the vote-trade offer and it sealed his hang. The tip was right. Grace later followed it ('No PMs between us').

tips_feedback.tip: Open every night-chat message with 'Holder: X. Target: Y. My action: Z.'
tips_feedback.why: Every Yakuza message used the format. All four votes landed on the target every night, so no kill was lost to a split vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover in Night 1 chat: a real Village role that fits your tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza assigned passive covers (Fortune Teller, Scout, Tracker) on Night 1. Grace's Scout claim and Erin's Tracker will held up until mechanics caught them (a census and an Enforcer kill). Bob's extra Notorious claim was not part of the plan and is what the census broke.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first night they can swing something; they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: Niaj spent a token on Night 3 and killed the Katana holder. Players who ignored the tip lost value: Olivia died with her Seer token unspent and Ivan with both mirrors unspent.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer, Arsonist or Werewolf cause proves that killer is alive. From Day 2 keep a written Neutral-killer suspect list: quiet claimants nobody has watched... While two Yakuza may be alive near the lock, give the hang to your Yakuza lead.
tips_feedback.why: The Werewolf causes on Night 2 proved a Werewolf was alive, and Carol was exactly the quiet claimant nobody watched. On Day 4 the town hanged a Neutral instead of Grace, its Yakuza lead, and lost. The tip was right, and ignoring it cost the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Run a Jester check before every hang... keep power roles on Innocent, since every Guilty voter is a ticket in the revenge draw.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory, a Hitman, knew this caution and used it with a fake Jester claim to win an Innocent verdict on Day 3. Carol, the Werewolf, gave revenge-draw fear as her reason for Innocent, which gave her safe cover. When Mallory was hanged on Day 4, no Jester win was announced, which showed the claim had been false all along.

issues.description: Night 5: only Carol was alive besides Olivia, so the Seer's random pair of two other players couldn't be drawn. The Seer text doesn't cover this case; the Census Taker's text does ('the group is smaller'). The moderator flagged it and gave no result, which was sensible, but the rule should say what happens.

The Informant text says it sees 'how every player voted' and doesn't say whether that is the vote cast or the vote as counted. The Fixer and Merciful texts are what imply it reports the counted vote. In Bob's trial Mallory (Merciful) said 'Guilty' in public, but the Informant report showed Innocent. Erin and Grace concluded she had lied about her vote and planned Day 4 around that. The ruling was correct, but the Informant's own text should say it reports votes as counted.

On Day 3 Carol said the only Village roles with no night action are Saint, Mayor and Sniper. She left out Magistrate and the passive-result roles (Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout, Bloodhound need no action), so her case against Mallory's 'no night action' claim was stronger than the rules support.
